newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies seen frost free to Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies seen frost free to Saturday.

text.p: Canada's Prairies Tuesday were forecast to be free of any risk of frost over any significant areas until Saturday, Environment Canada said.
"Saturday it starts to cool off and there's a moderate risk of frost for northern Alberta and a slight risk north of Edmonton and maybe in the foothills," meteorologist Gerald Machnee told Reuters.

The Prairies saw overnight lows Tuesday of 9.0 Celsius except in Coronation, Alberta, with a low of 2.8 C (37.0 F) at chest level for four hours and Wasagaming, Manitoba, which saw a low of 3.7 C (38.7 F) for two hours.
Ground level temperatures may be 2.0 to 5.0 C lower depending on how much insulating moisture there is and how strong winds are.
"There was a lot of dew in both places and calm winds in Wasagaming and winds of 15 to 17 kilometers an hour in Coronation, so not much," Machnee said.
Lows Prairie-wide were expected to remain around 9.0 C through to Saturday, he said.
"Sunday, there's a slight risk of frost in the far north of Alberta but it heats back up again Monday," he said.
